author: Asia Today and translated by UPI
title: Lee says political system fueled housing speculation - NewsBreak
text:
By Asia Today and translated by UPI ,
11 hours ago Feb. 18 (Asia Today) -- President Lee Jae-myung said Tuesday that distortions in South Korea's housing market stem from political decisions that enabled speculation, not from multiple home ownership itself.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung speaks during a Cabinet meeting at the presidential office Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, South Korea, 10 February 2026. Photo by YONHAP / EPA Lee wrote on X, formerly Twitter, that if lawmakers with authority to design and enforce laws granted advantages that made speculative multi-home ownership profitable, "that is the problem."
His remarks came after People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok criticized Lee for appearing to demonize multi-homeowners in a previous post about tightening regulations.
Lee said he does not view multi-home ownership itself as a social evil but argued that the political system failed to make speculative ownership sufficiently burdensome. "The law, representing the minimum standard of morality, must be limited to what must be strictly observed," he wrote, adding that violations should carry strict consequences.
The administration is reviewing additional tax and financial measures, including ending a temporary suspension of heavier capital gains taxes on multi-homeowners and tightening loan regulations, Asia Today reported. The stated goal is to shift the market toward actual housing demand rather than investment demand.
Lee also stressed that not all multi-home ownership would be targeted. He cited rural homes where parents reside or second homes in areas facing depopulation as examples that would not be treated as speculative.
In parallel with real estate measures, the government is preparing policies aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures, including reviewing pricing structures for daily necessities and addressing school uniform costs, according to the report.
-- Reported by Asia Today; translated by UPI
